physical.notes: The cabinet/coin door wiring diagram (PDF page 126) draws the Memory Protect Switch, N.O., from CPU board CN6 pin 12 (BLK-RED). se.c's ram_w refuses writes to the protected RAM while public -3 is 1, and sega.vbs names the address swMemoryProtect; a closed coin door is public -3 at 1 and an open door 0. The Diagnostic Aids page: opening the Coin Door after a CMOS RAM failure 'will initiate a Factory Restore (Reset), by opening the Memory Protect Switch'.

The cabinet wiring diagram draws it, N.O., among the PORTALS™ SERVICE BUTTONS on the coin door.

The opto board pages state the construction: with light on the receiver its output transistor is off and acts as an OPEN SWITCH, and when the beam is blocked it conducts and acts as a CLOSED SWITCH (OPTO Troubleshooting: 'CLOSED OPTO (Light Blocked) = SWITCH CLOSED'), so the contact rests open and a ball in the beam reads 1. Placement from the retained table's Kicker BallRelease (projection: cvpmBallStack bsTrough (InitSw 0, 14, 13, 12, 11) has no switch objects; projected onto its release kicker BallRelease). physical.location: playfield, on the right flipper assembly
physical.notes: Printed dedicated switch DS-4 (#4 RIGHT FLIPPER E.O.S. (End-of-Stroke)), wired GRY-YEL to CN6-P6 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. The grid prints its mounting 'Below Playfield' and its part '180-5149-00 on Flipper'; the 2-Flipper Circuit Wiring Diagram (PDF page 124) draws it 'ON ASSY.' as an N.C. switch, and the right Flipper Assembly (500-6682-02) lists the EOS switch 180-5149-00. The diagram explains that the switch opens about 1/16" when the flipper is energized and that the CPU applies another 40 ms pulse when it sees the switch close during a hold. normally_closed records that construction: at rest the contact is closed. PinMAME does not pass that level through: term3 declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) | FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L), core.h defines FLIP_SOL(x) to include FLIP_EOS(x), and core.c's flipper update therefore rewrites this input on every update, 0 while the flipper solenoid is off and 1 once it has been on for CORE_FLIPSTROKETIME (2) updates. PinMAME's model reads open at rest and closed at the end of the stroke, the opposite of the construction, and a host write never reaches the ROM: in the Dedicated Switch Test run holding it left the display at NONE, and in the gameplay run host writes of 1 and 0 to the left end-of-stroke input 83 while the left flipper button was held changed no output. A consumer receives PinMAME's simulated level and need not write this input. The retained script never writes it; sega.vbs names this address swURFlip, an upper-flipper label it writes only when an upper flipper solenoid is registered, which the retained table does not do. Placement from the retained table's Flipper RightFlipper (projection: the end-of-stroke contact sits on the flipper assembly; projected onto the flipper the table animates). The term3 ROM's Dedicated Switch Test prints "NONE" while the host holds it.

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls (the front page requires four pinballs) rest in the 4-Ball Trough 500-6318-14 on micro switches 11 (left), 12 and 13 and at the up-kicker on the VUK opto 14; the trough's Dual OPTO boards carry 14 and the stacking opto 15. Q1 (26-1200) kicks the ball on 14 up into the shooter lane and the rest roll one place toward the up-kicker. Hold each occupied position at 1 and pass the kicked ball through 15 as a short 1 pulse (beam blocked). In the ball-serve run the ROM fired Q1 0.7 s after the game-on state rose; in the gameplay run, where the scenario put a ball on 16 before the ROM served one, it never fired Q1. In the stacking-opto run, with four balls on 11-14 in attract mode, raising 15 to 1 made the ROM fire Q1 six times about 0.8 s apart and then the auto launch Q2 once, 9.1 s after the rise; lowering it fired nothing and raising it again repeated the pattern. The retained table's bsTrough never writes 15.
mechanisms.label: 4-ball trough with up-kicker and stacking opto

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball comes to rest on the shooter-lane rollover 16 in front of the Ball Auto Launch Assembly 500-6668-00, whose Q2 (22-1080) fires it up the lane onto the shooter-lane steel ramp. The player fires it with the gun on the cabinet front (Gun Shooter Connector Assembly 500-5698-02-79, trigger micro switch 55); an operator may fit the Ball Launch Button 500-6709-06-79 with its lamp 79 instead. In the ball-serve run Q1 served the ball, the scenario emptied the trough opto 14 and let the next ball block it, and the ROM held the served ball on 16 for 10 s and fired Q2 81 ms after the trigger was pulled, then 1.67 s and 3.34 s after that. In the gameplay run the scenario closed 16 before the ROM had served a ball and left 14 blocked; the ROM never fired Q1 and fired Q2 0.76 s later without a trigger pull, then every 1.6-1.7 s while the ball stayed on 16 and once 43 ms after the trigger was pulled, seven times in all, the last 0.18 s after the ball left. The record does not claim which condition makes the ROM launch on its own. The Diagnostic Aids page: the CPU activates the auto launch about ten times while 16 stays closed before it reports an Operator Alert. In both runs the ROM blinked lamp 79 from just after the game-on state rose until about 1.4-1.6 s after the trigger was pulled. The retained table fires a cvpmImpulseP from the trigger swplunger.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane, gun trigger and auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: Laser Kick Back Assembly 500-6697-01: 'When energized, kicks ball back into play from the Left Outlane', with a 23-800 coil. In the gameplay run closing the left outlane 57 once fired Q12. The ROM, not a wire, decides whether it is armed; lamp 37 is printed KICK BACK. The retained table fires a plunger object and pulls it back on release.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: VUK Left Style Assembly 500-6290-00: a ball resting on the heavy-duty micro switch 36 is kicked by Q13 (26-1200); 'Ball launches into the VUK Chute above the Playfield onto the Wire Ramp'. In the Switch Test run closing 36 fired Q13, and in the gameplay run a ball resting on it drew Q13 with the drop-target coils 3 and 8 and flasher 30. The retained table catches the ball in tophole and kicks it out of vukout.
mechanisms.label: VUK

mechanisms.behavior: The TX Cannon Trough 500-6655-00 at the T-X figure holds up to three balls: lockup 1 (right) on the single opto 33, lockup 2 and lockup 3 (left) on micro switches 34 and 35; the location drawing puts the above-playfield switch 31 (T-X MADE) beside them, and both retained scripts pulse 31 as the ball enters the lockup. The trough 'works with' the TX Vertical Up-Kicker 500-6656-00, whose Q14 (26-1200) kicks the ball up into the T-X cannon's wire ramp; IPDB: 'T-X ball cannon (shoots ball at right flipper)'. In the Switch Test run closing 33, 34 or 35 fired Q14. In the gameplay run a ball resting on 33 drew Q14 with the backbox switched G.I. 4 and flashers 26 and 30 and blinked the G.I. The retained table stacks the balls in bstxhole and kicks them out of tvukout.
mechanisms.label: T-X cannon lockup and up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: 1-Bank Drop Target 500-6440-01: one target on the micro switch 25 (180-5158-00), raised by the reset coil Q3 (27-1500) and knocked down by the mini trip coil Q8 (32-1250, 515-6916-01); the page includes a target-height adjustment. The ROM drives both coils as game logic: it fired Q3 at power-up, on Start, after the drain and with several scoring switches, and Q8 three times from about 1.6 s after the gun trigger launched the ball, when backbox target 43 closed and when the target went down and came back up. The retained table's cvpmDropTarget holds 25 at 1 while the target is down.
mechanisms.label: 1-bank drop target

mechanisms.behavior: Ball Deflector Assemblies 500-6657-00 (Qty. 2), each with a 26-1200 coil: 'When energized, it deflects the ball into the Top VUKs or Top Lanes'. The coil chart calls them the LEFT UP POST (Q22) and CENTER UP POST (Q23); DR. 7 draws 22 at the T-X figure and 23 behind the bumpers. Neither has a switch of its own. In the gameplay run each orbit switch (24, 28, 29, 46) made the ROM hold both on for about 2.1 s, the second starting 0.2-0.5 s after the first. The retained table raises the walls LeftPost and CenterPost while each is energized.
mechanisms.label: Left and center up posts (ball deflectors)

mechanisms.behavior: The back panel carries a wire ramp (535-9241-00) into a back-channel trough and the Kicker (Ball Stop) Assembly 500-6219-01 (26-1200, Q21, which the coil chart names BACK PANEL DIVERTER): 'When energized, the ball is held in Back Channel Trough on the Back Panel'. The skill-shot switch 52 sits behind the back panel under that trough. In the gameplay run closing 52 once fired Q21. The retained table models the stop as two walls on the playfield's rear edge that Q21 swaps.

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB: 'Backbox reciprocating cannon shoots Delrin Ball horizontally at 5 targets'. In the backbox insert, Q20 drives the Relay (Picker) & Cable Assembly 500-6700-00, which runs a 24V AC 21 RPM motor (041-5079-01); its eccentric Drive Wheel 535-9277-01 moves the RPG cannon's kicker bracket up and down, so the cannon sweeps its arc. The RPG Cannon Kicker Assembly 500-6697-00 (23-800, Q5) shoots the cannon's own ball into the five Stand-Up Targets 41 (top) to 45 (bottom). The grid lists no switch for the cannon's position. The front page: 'Remove Shipping Post Ref. A from the Backbox Insert under the RPG Cannon before Powering Up'. The RPG Backbox Test runs the motor through one full cycle, fires the kicker from the gun trigger (or the optional auto-launch button) and lights the insert lamps 65-69; the switched G.I. Q4 lights eight lamps in the centre of the arc and Q27/Q28 flash four lamps on each side. In the gameplay run closing each target once drew neither Q5 nor Q20; only the Single Coil Test fired them. The retained table fires its backbox kicker only while its own ball is in the backbox and runs a timer from Q20.
mechanisms.label: RPG backbox cannon and targets

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q9/49), right (Q10/50) and bottom (Q11/51) bumpers with 26-1200 coils and stack switches 180-5015-03; the G.I. circuit V lights all three ('GIs in Pop Bumpers (X3)'), each with one #555 wedge-base bulb on the bumper assembly page, which the G.I. wiring page counts as #44. mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q17/59) and right (Q18/62) slingshots, Slingshot Assemblies 500-5849-00 with 23-800 coils and two parallel blade contacts per side; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay run.

mechanisms.behavior: Left (500-6682-12) and right (500-6682-02) flipper assemblies, both with 22-1080 coils, on one 50v supply. The CPU applies a 40 ms pulse on a button closure and then 1 ms every 12 ms while the button is held; each N.C. end-of-stroke switch opens at full stroke, and a closure during a hold earns another 40 ms pulse. PinMAME publishes Q15 at 47/48 and Q16 at 45/46 and writes the end-of-stroke inputs 81 and 83 itself from the solenoid state.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: UK only: the Solenoid Expander Auxiliary board 520-5068-01 drives AUX 1 and AUX 3, the left and right outlane Ball Deflector Assemblies 500-5788-02, and AUX 2, the center Up/Down Post Assy 500-6293-00 between the flippers. The Post Save buttons under the flipper buttons ask the ROM for them: the left button (1) the left deflector, the right button (8) the right one, both together the center post. A standard machine fits none of them; on term3's default settings the gameplay run's button holds fired none.
mechanisms.label: UK Post Save deflectors and center post

physical.notes: Coils Detailed Chart Table (DR. 6) row #1 "TROUGH UP-KICKER": drive transistor Q1, cell "26-1200 / 090-5044-00B". The 4-Ball Trough 500-6318-14 carries this 26-1200 coil under the up-kicker. Retained table script: Solcallback(1) = "bstrough.solout" (line 310) kicks the trough ball stack out of BallRelease (lines 72-78). In the harness runs the ROM fired it 0.7 s after the game-on state rose in the ball-serve run, and in the stacking-opto run six times, about 0.8 s apart, each time 15 was raised in attract mode; in the gameplay run, where the scenario put a ball on 16 before the ROM served one, it never fired. Coils Detailed Chart Table (DR. 6) row #2 "AUTO LAUNCH": drive transistor Q2, cell "22-1080 / 090-5032-00B". The Ball Auto Launch Assembly 500-6668-00 (22-1080 coil) works with the gun shooter. Retained table script: Solcallback(2) = "Auto_plunger" (line 311) fires the cvpmImpulseP plungerIM on the shooter-lane trigger swplunger (PlungerIM.AutoFire, lines 294-304). In the harness runs in the stacking-opto run it fired once, 9.1 s after each rise of 15 in attract mode, after the six fires of 1; in the ball-serve run the served ball rested on 16 for 10 s and the ROM fired it 81 ms after the gun trigger 55 was pulled, then again 1.67 s and 3.34 s after that; in the gameplay run, where the ball reached 16 before the ROM served one, it fired 0.76 s later without a trigger pull, then every 1.6-1.7 s while the ball stayed on 16 and once 43 ms after the gun trigger was pulled, seven times in all, the last 0.18 s after the ball left. Placement from the retained table's Trigger swplunger (projection: cvpmImpulseP plungerIM fires from the shooter-lane trigger swplunger). The term3 ROM's Single Coil Test prints "#2 AUTO LAUNCH / YEL-VIO BRN-RED" for Q2, and firing it there pulsed public 2.

physical.notes: One G.I. relay on the I/O Power Driver Board 520-5137-01 (U206 74HCT273 data latch output D0 through R254 1K and the Q200 2N3904 relay driver, coil on 20v DC with D229 1N4004 across it) switches the 5.7v AC G.I. supply from J14 to four separately fused circuits on J15 (General Illumination Circuit Detailed Wiring Diagram, PDF page 121): B, F24, BRN-WHT to WHT-BRN, 'Back Panel X10, Insert X6, and above Playfield X2', 16 #44 and 2 #555; Y, F25, YEL to WHT-YEL, 'Left & Lower Playfield X18', 18 #44; G, F26, GRN to WHT-GRN, 'Backbox Insert X17 + US Coin Door X2 (Euro X1)', 17 #44 and 2 #555 on the coin door; V, F27, VIO to WHT-VIO, 'Right Playfield X20', 20 #44 including 'GIs in Pop Bumpers (X3)'. The page warns that G.I. bulb quantities may change during production, and its text layer also carries 'Note: GI above P/F is #555 Bulb.', which the rendered page does not show. The bumper assembly page (PDF page 101) names the bumper bulb more specifically: item 1, '#555 Wedge Base Bulb' 165-5002-00, one per bumper, labelled 'Gen. Illum. (GI) X3'. So the three pop-bumper G.I. bulbs that the wiring page counts among circuit V's #44 bulbs are #555 on the assembly page; both readings are kept, and the circuit counts below follow the wiring page. The quantity 75 is the four circuits' printed bulbs: 40 at the playfield (the two above-playfield reflector bulbs pointing at the T-X and T-850 figures among them), ten on the back panel's light board, 23 in the backbox insert and two on the coin door. se.c publishes the relay as GI 0; in the harness runs the ROM switched it on during boot, blinked it after Start, with the right 3-bank 22, the captive ball 23 and T-X made 31 and while a ball sat at lockup 1 (33), and switched it off at the drain. Retained table script: UseGI = 0 (line 24), but line 1250 sets GICallback to GIUpdate, which switches every member of the GIGruppe collection with G.I. 0 (lines 1252-1255). Its 68 render-double clusters of GIGruppe Lights give 43 sockets that draw a bulb mesh, each placed, observed only, on its bulb Light; the 25 clusters that draw no bulb are render helpers and are not placed. 5 of the placed sockets lie within 0.07 of the rear edge, where the back panel's ten-bulb light board stands; the circuit letters have not been matched to the sockets, so no placement carries a string, and the placements are not a one-to-one census of the 40 playfield bulbs.
